instruction: Denise, Glenn and I went on a trip recently. Yesterday, Denise emailed me their expenses in a pdf. Forward that thread to Glenn with an additional attachment of "~/documents/personal/expenses_james.pdf" from my file system, and a note prefixed to its body, "Can you please take care of splitting expenses? PFA for both of our expenses.".
notes: Apps: supervisor, phone (contact lookup for Denise's and Glenn's emails), gmail, file_system (token needed for uploading the attachment). Flow: find Denise's thread in the inbox (from_email filter, yesterday, pdf attachment), inspect it, forward the thread to Glenn as a draft (draft_not_send=true), read the draft body, update the draft body so it starts with the required note followed by the original forwarded content, upload ~/documents/personal/expenses_james.pdf to the draft with the file_system token, then send the draft. This yields exactly one new email (response to Denise's email, forwarded subject/body) with one new attachment and no file-system modifications. Static init facts (contact-email, thread-from, query-for) are modeling links to placeholder objects whose concrete values are bound at runtime; no ids are known initially. supervisor-complete-task takes the thread and recipient as non-API record parameters so its precondition mirrors the goal; it is forced last via (task-completed).

plan: (gmail-forward-email-thread denise-expenses-thread glenn-email file-system-token true forward-draft glenn)
